clue.text: Destructive people train to break up exhibition

parts.note: demons are wicked, destructive beings

indicators.note: break up means the letters of train and to are broken apart and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Vandals wreck a train as a form of protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break up' rearranges TRAIN and TO into TRATION, which follows DEMONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a display or show, as of a product or skill.

clue.text: Papal appointee literary hacks recommend?

parts.note: a devil is a hack writer doing drudge work for another author
to advocate is to recommend or urge

explanation.surface: Which writers would a pope's official favour?
explanation.walkthrough: The devil's advocate was the Vatican official who argued against a proposed canonisation; read as a phrase, it is hack writers backing something.
explanation.definitionFit: The Promotor Fidei, popularly so called, was appointed by the Pope to argue against candidates for sainthood.

clue.text: Hawthorn blossom's pronounced suitable for animal feed

indicators.note: says the word for hawthorn blossom is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: hawthorn flowers are called may, so the blossom's is may's

explanation.surface: Is hawthorn blossom said to be good fodder for cattle?
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is widely grown as fodder for livestock.

clue.text: Omitting to genuflect, perhaps, before start of Litany?

definitions.note: here omitting stands for an adjective, careless or remiss in doing

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word genuflect is to be taken loosely, its letters reordered
start of takes only the opening letter of the word Litany

explanation.surface: A churchgoer forgets to bend the knee before prayers begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges GENUFLECT into NEGLECTFU; 'start of' adds the L of Litany. 'Omitting to' is a participle standing for the adjective: omitting to = careless about.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone remiss or forgetful about duties fails to do them.

clue.text: A month in class upset hard workers

indicators.note: in places the month inside the turned-round word for class
upset in a down clue turns the word for class upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a sort is a class or kind
a month here is January, abbreviated Jan

explanation.surface: A month of disrupted classes troubles diligent staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SORT into TROS, and JAN goes inside it. To 'work like a Trojan' is to work very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil like a Trojan is an idiom for working tirelessly, so tireless toilers are so named.

clue.text: A US city sage appears, no matter how

parts.note: NY is short for New York
a sage is wise

explanation.surface: A wise man shows up in New York, however he manages it.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning in any way or manner at all.

clue.text: Soldiers in denim picking off foes

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words denim picking

explanation.surface: Troops in jeans shoot down enemies one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'denIM PIcking'; 'off foes' completes the picture of a fighting force.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment or band of warriors.

clue.text: Student goes into assembly — one starting a new term

indicators.note: assembly means the letters are put together afresh in another order

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A pupil enters the school hall as the new term begins.
explanation.walkthrough: L joins the letters of GOES INTO, and 'assembly' rearranges the lot. The definition plays on term as a word rather than a school period.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiner of fresh words introduces novel vocabulary.

clue.text: Castaway spotted birds on erratic course

parts.note: robins are birds

indicators.note: erratic means the word course is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A shipwrecked sailor sees birds flying a wandering path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratic' rearranges COURSE into CRUSOE; ROBINS + ON precede it. Defoe's hero is the classic castaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's hero was marooned for years on a desert island.

clue.text: Such braggadocio made Livy groan

indicators.note: made suggests the words Livy and groan are made over into another arrangement

explanation.surface: The Roman historian moaned at boastful bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges the letters of LIVY and GROAN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive pride and boastfulness are the same vice.

clue.text: Rejected work includes spicy picture

indicators.note: includes means the word for work holds the next piece within it
rejected means the short word for work is sent back, reading backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
spicy food is hot

explanation.surface: A turned-down piece of art contains a racy image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns OP into PO, which 'includes' HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot taken with a camera is an image.

clue.text: Lair for animal about to leave cage in Belgium

parts.note: a lie is where an animal lies, its lair

indicators.note: to leave says some letters go out of the word cage

parts.note: ca is circa, about

explanation.surface: A creature's den, after it escapes its cage, is in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes CA (circa) out of CAGE, leaving GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in eastern Wallonia, on the Meuse.

clue.text: Fine article about king, possibly written by Boito

indicators.note: about places the first piece around the letter for king

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
R is rex, king
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A good piece on a monarch, perhaps by the Italian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Arrigo Boito was an Italian composer and librettist.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo song is the kind of thing an opera composer writes.

clue.text: In the same book Bashan's king returned to the desert

indicators.note: returned turns both short pieces back to front where they stand

parts.note: ib is short for ibidem, in the same place or book
Og was the biblical king of Bashan

explanation.surface: The same biblical book tells of Bashan's ruler going back to the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns IB to BI and OG to GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast arid region of Mongolia and China.

clue.text: Progress more, say, as one in loco parentis

indicators.note: say signals the phrase is heard as spoken, in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: to progress further is to step farther

explanation.surface: Advancing further as a guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: In loco parentis is Latin for in the place of a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother's husband takes the role of parent to her children.

clue.text: Evergreen only found in a Latin country

indicators.note: found in places the word for only inside the Latin word

parts.note: rus is Latin for countryside
but means only

explanation.surface: A tree that grows only in one Latin nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry tree is a broadleaf shrub that keeps its leaves all year.

clue.text: Sinister young woman's kidnapped slave

parts.note: black can mean sinister or evil
bird is British slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: An evil girl has abducted a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackbirding was the kidnapping of Pacific Islanders for forced labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Islanders seized for forced plantation labour were so called in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Records of actors' appearances

explanation.surface: Logs of performers' stage arrivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Items written in a ledger, and the moments players come on stage.

clue.text: Railway supporter comes by tube

parts.note: via means by way of
a duct is a tube or pipe

explanation.surface: A rail fan arrives on the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests London's Underground, but it is just a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A long bridge carries a railway across a valley.

clue.text: First to hold sway, before she fell?

indicators.note: to hold means the word for first wraps round the word for sway

parts.note: top means first or foremost
to roll is to sway from side to side

explanation.surface: She was supreme before her downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a 'fallen woman' is a loose one, a woman who has fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: A promiscuous woman was called fallen in Victorian moral language.

clue.text: Revolutionary device for receiving cables at sea

definitions.text: Revolutionary device for receiving cables at sea

parts.words: Revolutionary device for receiving cables at sea
parts.note: revolutionary suggests politics but means turning round; cables are ropes hauled in, not telegrams

explanation.definitionFit: A rotating drum on a ship winds in heavy ropes and anchor chains.

clue.text: Excuse prisoner already committed

parts.note: con is short for convict
something already committed has been done

explanation.surface: Pardoning a convict for a crime already carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook an offence is to forgive it.

clue.text: Source of heat acceptable in church

indicators.note: in places the word for acceptable inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: Heating that is fine in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuel made from coal burns hot and smokeless.

clue.text: Blue feathers

explanation.surface: Sad plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Depressed or low in spirits, and soft fine plumage under a bird's outer layer.

clue.text: Poet's claim to be at all times a Muslim ruler

parts.note: I am is the claim to be
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, flagged by Poet's

explanation.surface: A poet boasts that he will forever be an emir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' warns that the form is poetic: E'ER for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of emir, a prince or commander in Islamic lands.

clue.text: The Spanish boy in "The Lady of the Lake"?

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
Len is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Is the Spanish lad a character in Scott's poem?
explanation.walkthrough: Ellen Douglas is the heroine of Walter Scott's poem The Lady of the Lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's heroine Ellen Douglas is the title lady of that poem.

clue.text: Inequalities not even Socrates initially recognized

parts.note: an odd number is not even

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the name Socrates

explanation.surface: Even Socrates did not notice some imbalances.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparities or unequal amounts, as in fighting against the odds.

clue.text: Sound attempt — total three

indicators.note: sound says the following words are heard spoken aloud

parts.note: a try is an attempt; to add is to total

explanation.surface: A good effort, adding up to three.
explanation.definitionFit: A group or set of three things.

clue.text: Means of evasion employed by archers

explanation.surface: Ways out used by bowmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaps in a rule that let one dodge it, and narrow slits in castle walls for shooting arrows.

clue.text: Underworld aspect of the Mary Celeste crew

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld
aspect means appearance or look

explanation.surface: A hellish look about the crew of the ghost ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mary Celeste was found adrift in 1872 with her crew vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship's crew vanished without trace, the fate the definition points to.
